terms.grammar: adjective and pronoun; dat. aliī; for the genitive alterīus is usual
evidence: Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.19: nē mīrēre aliā manū esse
terms.comment: Another of a different kind, place or person: aliā viā, another way. Alius atque alius, one after another (Liv. 1.8.4). For “something else, someone else”, see else.

terms.grammar: adjective and pronoun; gen. alterīus, dat. alterī
terms.comment: A second of the same kind: alter īdem, a second self. Of a pair, “the other” (see the other).

phrases.latin: Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.
phrases.english: That way didn’t work; we’ll try another.

phrases.latin: haec inter cēnam Tīrōnī dictāvī, nē mīrēre aliā manū esse
phrases.english: I dictated this to Tiro at dinner, so don’t be surprised that it is in another hand

phrases.latin: est enim is quī est tamquam alter īdem
phrases.english: for a friend is, as it were, a second self

phrases.latin: jam hortum ipsī agricolae succīdiam alteram appellant
phrases.english: and the farmers themselves call the vegetable garden their second side of bacon

phrases.latin: crēscēbat interim urbs mūnītiōnibus alia atque alia appetendō loca
phrases.english: meanwhile the city kept growing, taking in one place after another with its walls
